## The software is ready — http://maker:4000

I've switched from facilitator to implementer and built the real, running application in `implementation/` (a Node.js web app with durable SQLite storage and a responsive browser UI), working from the approved behaviours — not the exploration prototypes.

## Verification report (all passed)

I verified the implementation against the approved scenarios' behaviour and with internal tests: **42 automated tests pass** — covering the search query language, duplicate-detection rules, import/export round-trip, the data layer, and an end-to-end pass over the running app for each scenario.

- **Honest note:** verification *found one defect*, and I fixed it before presenting: the "select all that match" bulk action was targeting the wrong scope in one case. It's corrected and covered by a test now.
- **Two fidelity notes, stated plainly:** a preserved page copy is saved as a single self-contained HTML file (deeper asset-inlining is a future enhancement); and auto-fill, copies, and Internet Archive depend on network reachability — when a page can't be reached, the app degrades to exactly the approved fallback/failure states rather than failing the save.

## What's implemented (the 17 approved behaviours)

Effortless save with reviewed auto-fill · tags + formatted note · full search language (`#tag`, `"phrases"`, `AND/OR/NOT`, clickable tags) · To read / Finished / All (+ status at save/edit) · Archive vs confirmed Delete · duplicate → edit the existing one · open original in a new tab · multi-select bulk actions incl. select-all-matching · automatic preserved copies + optional Internet Archive · live collections · import/export · display preferences · plus the first-run, empty, long-content, large-library, and edge-case behaviours.

You can open **http://maker:4000** and try it — it starts on the empty first-run state, so pasting a link and pressing **Save** is a good first step.

I've also recorded, for a **later cycle**, the one idea that would go beyond the approved scope: automatic dead-link detection (in `context/later-cycle-requests.md`).
